running_header.center: Cenſura trium Theologorum Anglorum, extrà collegium commorantium

layout_note: Single column. The LAST printed (text) leaf of the 1610 OT2 (Second Tome), a verso printed '1124' — a SECOND, distinct end-of-volume approbation, separate from the front-matter Douai-Doctors 'APPROBATIO.' (matter-ot2-approbatio, p.2). This one is the censure of THREE ENGLISH theologians resident OUTSIDE the college. It sits at the very end of the back matter, immediately after the alphabetical index 'A Particular Table of the Most Principal Things' (which ends 'FINIS' on the preceding recto, printed p.1123 / index 1125); the following leaf (index 1127) is a blank endpaper. Top: a two-line ITALIC display title 'Cenſura trium Theologorum Anglorum, extrà collegium commorantium' (= 'Censure of three English Theologians, dwelling outside the college'), with the printed page number '1124' set at the far top-left. Below it: one ROMAN-body Latin paragraph of 14 type-lines opening 'NOs infraſcripti…' and closing with the year '1609.' (no month/day, unlike the front APPROBATIO's 'Duaci. 8. Nouembris. 1609.'). At foot: three signatory blocks, each two lines, in roman small-caps names + roman/italic descriptors — (1) IOANNES WRIGHTVS, Dean of the collegiate church of the Glorious Virgin at Courtrai (Certracenſis); (2) MATTHEVS KELLISONVS, S.Th.D & Professor at Rheims (Remensi); (3) GVLIELMVS HARRISONVS, S.Th.D — all three 'aliquando Sacrarum Literarum in hoc Collegio Profeſſores' (formerly professors of Scripture in this [English] College). Like its OT2-approbatio sibling this is a CARELESSLY-set page with many compositor vowel/letter typos, preserved diplomatically (see uncertain): feteris (for Veteris), cumq; abbrev, Annotationabus (for -ibus), inſertio (for inſertis), Vtpotæ (for Vtpote), fidilem (for fidelem), temporem (for temporum), Paſtorem (for Paſtorum), Doctrinacque (for Doctrinæque), hereſies (for hæreſes), vniueſitate (for vniuerſitate), Sactarum (for Sacrarum), Glorioſ (for Glorioſæ). The page uses VARIABLE French spacing — a space before ';' and ':' in most clauses (and before a few commas), but not always (e.g. 'elucidant;hereſies' is tight). Type is Latin roman + italic only, so the vv-vs-w apparatus rule does not apply (no 'w' sort in Latin, no footnote face). A modern scanner watermark 'www.fatimamovement.com' and a small red heraldic shield are overlaid at the lower-left corner — NOT original, excluded; heavy ink foxing spots speckle the lower half. Being the last text page there is NO catchword.

intervals.text: Cenſura trium Theologorum Anglorum, extrà collegium commorantium

NOs infraſcripti, perlecta hac feteris Teſtamenti verſione, cum Librorum argumentis & capitum cumq; Annotationabus, ac Recapitulationibus ſuis, locis inſertio ; nihil inuenimus, quod fidei Catholicæ, aut bonis moribus repugnet ; ſed econtra reperimus tranſlationem fidilem ; reliqua docta & vtilia, Vtpotæ quæ exactam temporem ſeriem ; Eccleſiæ Paſtorem Doctrinacque Catholicæ ſucceſſionem, ab ipſo mundi exordio deducunt ; obſcuriora ſacri textus loca elucidant;hereſies huius temporis argumentis ex ipſo eodem textu collectis conuincunt ; Eccleſiæ Catholicæ dogmata penè omnia confirmant : Ideoq ; Summâ cum legentium vtilitate publicari poſſe indicamus : Si ordinarijs Librorum cenſoribus hoc ipſum approbari beneplacitum fuerit 1609.
IOANNES WRIGHTVS, Eccleſiæ collegiatæ Glorioſ Virginis, Certracenſis Decanus
MATTHEVS KELLISONVS, S. Theologiæ Doctor ac Profeſſor in vniueſitate Remensi.
GVLIELMVS HARRISONVS, S. Theologiæ Doctor, omnes aliquando Sactarum Literarum in hoc Collegio Profeſſores.

uncertain.note: Intended word is 'Veteris' (Veteris Teſtamenti = of the Old Testament). The printed sort is NOT a two-stroke 'V/v' but a single tall stem: at 5x it shows a crossbar through the stem, so read as 'f' → 'feteris'; a long-ſ (no crossbar) cannot be fully excluded at this raster ('ſeteris'). Either way it is a compositor error for 'Veteris'. Preserved as printed 'feteris'. Medium confidence on f-vs-ſ; high confidence it is a typo for Veteris.

The standard early-modern '-que' suspension: 'q' + a semicolon-like mark (with a faint macron over the q). Rendered 'cumq;' (= cumque, 'and with'); the same abbreviation recurs at line 13 as 'Ideoq;' (= Ideoque). The text has two 'cum' clauses: 'cum Librorum argumentis & capitum, cumque Annotationibus…'. High confidence on the expansion.

Split 'Anno-'(l.3)+'tationabus'(l.4). Printed ending '-abus' where correct Latin is '-ibus' (Annotationibus); the very next word 'Recapitulationibus' is set correctly with '-ibus', confirming this is a genuine compositor typo, not a misread. Preserved as printed. Medium-high confidence.

Split 'in-'(l.4)+'ſertio'(l.5). Reads 'inſertio'; correct Latin is 'inſertis' (locis inſertis = 'inserted in their proper places'). Probable dropped/mis-set final letters (-is → -io). Preserved as printed 'inſertio'. Medium confidence (foxing near the word).

Minor punctuation: a mark after 'inuenimus' reads as a comma but could be a foxing spot / faint stop; rendered as comma. The clause 'nihil inuenimus quod … repugnet' needs no internal stop. Low priority; the page is heavily speckled.
Printed 'Vtpotæ' with an æ ligature; correct Latin is 'Vtpote' (utpote, 'inasmuch as / seeing that'). Genuine typo (spurious æ). Preserved as printed. Medium-high confidence.
Split 'tranſ-'(l.6)+'lationem fidilem'(l.7). Printed 'fidilem' (i for e); correct Latin is 'fidelem' (tranſlationem fidelem = 'a faithful translation'). Preserved as printed. High confidence.
Printed 'temporem'; correct Latin is 'temporum' (exactam temporum ſeriem = 'an exact series of the times'). Preserved as printed. Medium-high confidence.

Printed 'Paſtorem'; correct Latin is 'Paſtorum' (Eccleſiæ Paſtorum … ſucceſſionem = 'the succession of the Pastors of the Church'). Parallel error to 'temporem' on the same line. Preserved as printed. Medium confidence.

Split 'Doctri-'(l.8)+'nacque'(l.9). Reads 'Doctrinacque' (n-a-c-q-u-e); correct Latin is 'Doctrinæque' (…Doctrinæque Catholicæ ſucceſſionem). The æ appears set as separate 'ac'. Preserved as printed. Medium confidence (ac vs æ).

Reads 'hereſies' (h-e-r-e-ſ-i-e-s); correct Latin is 'hæreſes' (the heresies of this time). Vowel typos (e for æ, extra i). Preserved as printed. Medium-high confidence. Note the following ';' is set TIGHT ('elucidant;hereſies') whereas most other ';'/':' on the page carry a leading French space.

Reads 'Summâ' with a circumflex over the final 'a' (ablative, 'Summâ cum … vtilitate' = 'with the greatest profit'). The circumflex is faint amid foxing. 'Ideoq ;' just before it = 'Ideoque'. High confidence on the word; medium on the diacritic shape.

Reads 'fuerit' (correct Latin, 'shall have been'). The initial shows a clear crossbar → 'f' (not long-ſ); calibrated against 'ſ' elsewhere on the page. High confidence. The year '1609.' follows and is clear.

Ioannes Wrightus (John Wright). Initial cap read as a single 'W'; a gapped 'VV' (display-cap convention) cannot be excluded at this size — render 'WRIGHTVS' / possibly 'VVRIGHTVS'. Also 'IOANNES' uses a capital I (DR I/J convention), though the sort has a J-like hook. Medium-high confidence on the name.

Line 16 ends 'Eccleſiæ collegiatæ Glorioſ' with the italic long-ſ and then blank measure — NO æ is set at the line end, so as-printed it is 'Glorioſ'. Correct Latin is 'Glorioſæ' ('Eccleſiæ collegiatæ Gloriosæ Virginis' = the collegiate church of the Glorious Virgin). Preserved as printed 'Glorioſ' (dropped/broken æ). Medium-high confidence the æ is absent.

Toponym for Courtrai / Kortrijk (Latin usually 'Cortracensis'); here printed with an 'e' in the first syllable, 'Certracenſis', possibly with a light accent over the 'e'. Ioannes Wrightus was Dean (Decanus) of the collegiate church of Our Lady there. Preserved as printed. Medium-high confidence.

Reads 'vniueſitate' (u/v-swap 'vni…'; long-ſ before 'itate') — the 'r' of 'vniuerſitate' is dropped (u-n-i-u-e-ſ-i-t-a-t-e, no r). Genuine typo, preserved as printed; = 'in vniuerſitate Remensi' (in the University of Rheims). 'Remensi' final 's' reads round (not long-ſ) at this size. Medium-high confidence on the missing r.

Gulielmus Harrisonus (William Harrison). Small-cap name reads 'GVLIELMVS'; the minim count between 'GV' and 'ELMVS' is ambiguous at this raster — could be 'GVILIELMVS' (Guilielmus, as the OT2/OT1 approbatio siblings set the analogous name). Preserved 'GVLIELMVS' as the closer reading; flag for review. Medium confidence.

Reads 'Sactarum' (S-a-c-t-a-rum, with a ct-cluster: the letter after 'c' rises above x-height with a crossbar = 't'); correct Latin is 'Sacrarum' ('Sacrarum Literarum' = of Sacred Letters/Scripture). Preserved as printed 'Sactarum' (probable t-for-r misprint); r-vs-t not 100% at this DPI. Medium confidence — flag for review.

glyph_counts.note: Approximate hand count over the page: ~26 long-ſ in the roman body paragraph (lines 2–15: infraſcripti, Teſtamenti, verſione, ſuis, inſertio, ſed, tranſlationem, ſeriem, Eccleſiæ ×2, Paſtorem, ſucceſſionem [ſſ], ipſo ×2, obſcuriora, ſacri, hereſies, poſſe [ſſ], cenſoribus, ipſum, …) + ~8 in the three signatory blocks (Eccleſiæ, Glorioſ, Certracenſi, Profeſſor [ſſ], vniueſitate, Profeſſores [ſſ]). 'feteris' (l.2) and 'fuerit' (l.15) are 'f' (crossbar), NOT long-ſ; small-cap names use round capital S (WRIGHTVS, KELLISONVS, HARRISONVS, Sactarum). Subject to script recompute; the transcription is the source of truth.

method: Four validations. (1) LOCALIZATION: paged the OT2 back matter via ocr-spike/jp2_page.py archive-ot2-1610 across ~998–1127. Mapped the region in order: canonical text ends and the italic 'Continuance of the Church / Church and Religion' recapitulation essay runs (indices ~1000–1004); the apocryphal appendix opens at index 1005 with 'The prayer of Manaſſes… are here placed after al the Canonical bookes… becauſe they are not receiued into the Canon' + the Prayer of Manasses, then THE THIRD BOOKE OF ESDRAS (index 1006+) and THE FOURTH BOOKE OF ESDRAS, ending 'FINIS' (index 1075); then the Table of Epistles (1076), the 24-leaf Historical Table (1077–1100), and the alphabetical 'A Particular Table of the Moſt Principal Things' index (1101–1125, ending 'FINIS'). The 'CENSVRA' is NOT within the scripture/table span; it is the LAST text leaf (index 1126), confirmed by grepping the project OCR layer (sources/our-ocr-diplomatic/archive-ot2-1610/…_1126.json) for censur/theolog/trium. The italic heading reads 'Cenſura trium Theologorum Anglorum, extrà collegium commorantium' and the body 'NOs infraſcripti…' — a censure/approbation, confirmed by heading + content. (2) IDENTITY: archive-ot2-1610 S1 = the 1610 Second Tome (jp2_page maps it to 'S01_1582-first-edition-3vol/…2 of 3 1610 Old Testament_jp2'); the surrounding leaves are unmistakably OT2 back matter (Historical Table 'The end of the ſixth age, and of the old Teſtament'; index 'of both the Tomes of the old Teſtament'); the censure is dated 1609, consistent with the 1610 OT2 imprint (approbations predate the title-page year, exactly as the front APPROBATIO's 'Duaci. 8. Nouembris. 1609.'). This is a SEPARATE item from matter-ot2-approbatio (Douai Doctors, p.2). (3) PLACEMENT: printed page number '1124' set top-left; it is the final printed (text) leaf — preceded by the index's 'FINIS' leaf (printed 1123 / index 1125) and followed by a blank endpaper (index 1127). No running header (the italic title occupies the top); no catchword (last page). (4) COMPLETENESS: the WHOLE section is on this one page — 2-line italic title + one 14-line roman Latin paragraph (closing '…fuerit 1609.') + three two-line signatory blocks (Ioannes Wrightus / Matthevs Kellisonus / Gvlielmus Harrisonus); nothing continues onto the blank following leaf. Read from the 400-DPI-class jp2 raster (native 3334×4684) with region crops zoomed 3–5x on the heading, both halves of the paragraph, and every signature line; diplomatic per GUIDELINES.md — long-ſ glyph-driven (feteris/fuerit resolved to 'f' by their crossbars; medial-s in body kept long-ſ), ct→component letters (docta, collectis, Doctor, collegiatæ), æ preserved, u/v period-swap kept (vtilia, vtilitate, vniueſitate, inuenimus, conuincunt, euulgari), i/j kept (IOANNES, ordinarijs), variable French spacing before ';'/':' preserved as seen, and this careless setting's many printer's typos preserved (see uncertain). The front-matter OT2 Approbatio GT was used only as a structural/formula anchor, never as a spelling oracle.
confidence: high on localization/identity/placement/completeness (all PASS) and on the italic title, the overall Latin paragraph, and the three signatory identities (Wright/Kellison/Harrison, dated 1609). Medium-to-high on the many diplomatically-preserved compositor typos, each flagged in uncertain (feteris→Veteris, Annotationabus→-ibus, inſertio→inſertis, Vtpotæ→Vtpote, fidilem→fidelem, temporem→temporum, Paſtorem→Paſtorum, Doctrinacque→Doctrinæque, hereſies→hæreſes, vniueſitate→vniuerſitate, Sactarum→Sacrarum, Glorioſ→Glorioſæ). Medium on two review-worthy readings at this raster limit: the 'GVLIELMVS'/'GVILIELMVS' minim count and the 'Sactarum' r-vs-t; and on minor foxing-affected punctuation/diacritics (the ';'/':' French spaces, 'Summâ' circumflex, 'penè' grave, 'extrà' grave, the comma after 'inuenimus').
glyph_regime_resolved: Latin roman + italic display/text only; NO w/vv regime on the page (Latin has no 'w' sort and there is no footnote/annotation face). Title = italic display (2 lines, with display suspension marks over 'trium'/'Theologorum' rendered as plain letters + accents 'extrà'/'Summâ'/'penè' preserved). Body = roman; the opening 'NOs' is a plain majuscule (N + small-cap O), NOT a woodcut drop-cap. Signatures = roman small-caps names (round capital S) + roman/italic descriptors. long-ſ resolved per glyph: present through the roman body and in italic 'Eccleſiæ'/'Glorioſ' and roman 'Profeſſor'/'Profeſſores'/'Certracenſi'/'vniueſitate'; the two 'f'-initials 'feteris' and 'fuerit' carry crossbars (f, not ſ). ct = always ligature (docta, collectis, Doctrinacque, Doctor, collegiatæ, Sactarum). æ preserved (Catholicæ, Eccleſiæ, Theologiæ, quæ, Vtpotæ, collegiatæ, Glorioſ[æ]); roman capitals would spell AE as two sorts (none needed here). u/v period-swap preserved (vtilia, vtilitate, vniueſitate, inuenimus, reperimus→no, conuincunt, euulgari→n/a, ipſum, IOANNES/WRIGHTVS/MATTHEVS/KELLISONVS/HARRISONVS/GVLIELMVS with V=U). i/j preserved (IOANNES, ordinarijs). Variable French spacing kept as printed (space before most ';'/':' but 'elucidant;hereſies' tight).
